analysis: Only two files changed, both documentation: changelog.d/nemotron-super-media-discovery.md (new, 64 lines) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (a 7-line Context paragraph on the unregistered Super builder's LOAD lease and concurrency floor). No source changes were supplied, so none of the described behavior was verified. The changelog describes provider-side changes on the TB-007 and TB-003 surfaces (T-041, T-028, T-050, T-012). (1) Consumer-supplied inline PNG/JPEG now decoded in-process by a CPU/ImageIO decoder, with EXIF/XMP orientation and declared-geometry bounds before allocation. Decoder memory-safety and DoS limits need source review. T-050 covers video temp-file plaintext, so confirm images do not touch disk. (2) An opt-in image/text HTTP hook, described as using existing auth and disabled by default. Check its bind address (loopback) and that it cannot bypass coordinator E2E decryption and request-scoping, since it adds a path to plaintext prompts in A-001. (3) The opt-in DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY RAM checkpoint bank, reported as a finding against T-041. (4) Env-controlled concurrency of up to 8, speculative MTP, and prefill chunks, which relate to the memory-admission invariants in hardware-support.md. The doc says the builder requires a live pending LOAD lease and keeps the fixed-workspace floor, which is consistent with the existing admission invariants. The model is described as unregistered and unqualified, so it should not be routable. Confirm that no registration or capability advertisement path (TB-002 / T-027) can expose it. Next pass should inspect NemotronSuperLocalBridgeBuilder.swift, the HTTP hook, the image decoder, and the prefix-cache salt keying.

findings.detail: The changelog says `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1` opts the Nemotron Super owner into exact text prefix reuse. It uses a resident recurrent checkpoint bank, sized from the KV grant (`min(1 GiB, grant/8)`), and reserved from load until retirement. T-041 and its mitigations say production never constructs or funds a resident-RAM prefix cache, that DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE is the single gate, and that the only tier is encrypted SSD with HMAC names, a 30-minute TTL and a KEK purge. A RAM bank is a second reuse path. It has no stated tie to the cacheSalt/account scoping, a different TTL, a different purge path, and a hit/miss TTFT oracle (SEC-035) that lives only in process memory and is not covered by at-rest encryption. Trigger: an operator sets the variable and the provider serves multi-account traffic. Impact: cross-tenant prefix-presence inference if reuse is not keyed by the coordinator-authored cacheSalt. I could not verify the source, so this is a documentation/threat-model gap and not a confirmed code flaw. Fix: update T-041 and TB-007 to cover this opt-in tier. State that it is default-off, that entries are keyed by cacheSalt, what the lifetime and purge are, and that it is cleared on unload. Confirm in source that the salt is part of the lookup key.
findings.title: Opt-in resident RAM prefix-cache bank contradicts T-041's 'no production RAM tier' assumption
